newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mixed in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mixed in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mixed in slow trading on Thursday as market trends remained unclear, traders said.
The most active May 1997 contract ended at 21,800 yuan ($2,627) per tonne, rising 40 yuan. It opened at 21,770 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 21,690 and a high of 21,880.
February was unchanged at 21,430, March fell 20 to 21,480, April 60 to 21,620, June 20 to 21,750, July 150 to 21,800, and August rose 10 to 21,860.
Combined volume fell to 21,390 tonnes from 25,820.
Traders said uncertainty about the direction of the market in the near term kept investors on the sidelines.
"Trading interest fell today, indicating that copper will not fluctuate sharply in the short term," one trader said.
"Profit-taking at high levels and support from the spot price at low levels will keep copper between 21,500 and 22,000," he added.
Traders said a lack of domestic market-moving news would see London Metals Exchange (LME) prices having a greater influence on the Shanghai copper market.
"Shanghai copper will follow the LME over the coming few days," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended mostly down on profit-taking. February rose 20 to 15,380, March fell 90 to 15,600, April 100 to 15,800 and May 50 to 16,000.
Combined volume fell to 690 tonnes from 1,820.
